Work began on the covering of the Senne, burying the polluted main river of Brussels to allow for urban renewal in the centre of the city.
U.S. secretary of state William H. Seward negotiated the purchase of Alaska from Russia for US$7.2 million.
Second French intervention in Mexico: Emperor Maximilian I of Mexico was executed by firing squad in Querétaro City.
The United States Congress established the Indian Peace Commission to seek peace treaties with a number of Native American tribes.

The first and second of three treaties were signed near Medicine Lodge, Kansas, between the United States federal government and several Native American tribes in the Great Plains, requiring them to relocate to areas in present-day western Oklahoma.
The Manchester Martyrs were hanged in Manchester, England, for involvement in a scheme to free two Irish nationalists from custody in which a police officer was killed.
In Angola, New York, the last coach of a Lake Shore Railway train derailed, plunged 40 feet (12 m) down a gully, and caught fire, resulting in approximately 49 deaths.
